extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic topology; advanced undergraduates studying cohomology and spectra
extracted.subtask_description: Describe/construct reduced cohomology theories from sequences of spaces (spectra), and the identification H^n(X;G) ≈ [X,K(G,n)] via a fundamental class. Includes the necessary conditions (loopspace structure, suspension isomorphisms) and the exactness machinery (Puppe sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an Ω–spectrum
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence of CW complexes K1, K2, … together with weak homotopy equivalences Kn → ΩKn+1 for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text allows replacing 'weak homotopy equivalence' by 'homotopy equivalence' (Milnor theorem makes Ω of a CW complex again of CW type). Omitting finitely many initial terms is harmless because earlier terms are reconstructed as CW approximations. An Ω–spectrum may be extended to negative indices and yields the suspension isomorphisms needed for a cohomology theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: When hn(X)=h(X,Kn) defines a reduced cohomology theory
rubrics_metrics.description: The functors hn(X) = h(X, Kn) will define a reduced cohomology theory provided the sequence {Kn} behaves like an Ω–spectrum (i.e. Kn ≃ ΩKn+1 up to weak equivalence), so that suspension isomorphisms and long exact sequences hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessities derived in the text: homotopy and wedge axioms follow easily; the long exact sequence is produced from Puppe/cofibration sequences and the weak equivalences Kn → ΩKn+1 permit continuation to the left to obtain exactness in all degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint relation (suspension/loopspace correspondence)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an adjoint bijection h(ΣX, K) = h(X, ΩK): basepoint-preserving maps ΣX → K correspond to basepoint-preserving maps X → ΩK.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relation is used to shift dimensions of homotopy groups (πn+1(K) = πn(ΩK)) and underlies why weak equivalences Kn → ΩKn+1 produce the suspension isomorphisms for the would-be cohomology theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for group structure on h(X,K)
rubrics_metrics.description: To give h(X,K) a group structure either X should be a suspension (ΣY) or K should be a loopspace ΩL; to be abelian (so the theory is graded-commutative/abelian from degree ≥2) K should be a double loopspace (Ω^2L) or, more generally, an n-fold loopspace for n ≥ 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If X = ΣY define the sum via collapsing an equatorial copy of Y; if K = ΩL use pointwise loop composition. Inverses arise from reflecting the suspension coordinate; iterating Ω gives abelian groups for higher degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy and wedge axioms imply additivity of induced maps
rubrics_metrics.description: If a functor h from basepointed CW complexes to abelian groups satisfies the homotopy and wedge axioms, then for basepoint-preserving maps f,g : X → K we have (f+g)^* = f^* + g^* (and the dual statement for covariant functors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 4.60: the proof uses the quotient collapsing an equatorial copy of X and the canonical maps i1,i2 and q1,q2 to compare (f∨g) and (f+g). This additivity is used to show degrees act by multiplication on cellular groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Puppe (cofibration) sequence produces exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting from an inclusion A ↪ X and iteratively attaching cones and forming suspensions produces the coﬁbration/Puppe sequence A → X → X ∪ CA → SA → SX → S(X ∪ CA) → … whose maps, after passing to homotopy classes into Kn (and using Kn→ΩKn+1), yield a long exact sequence of abelian groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When taking h(−, Kn) the first few terms are only sets but become groups from certain suspension stages onward; weak equivalences Kn→ΩKn+1 allow continuation leftwards indefinitely to get the full long exact sequence, and naturality follows from naturality of cofibration sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular chain/coboundary identification (homology/cohomology comparison)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a CW complex X the cellular chain complex arising from a generalized homology/cohomology theory h∗ agrees with the ordinary cellular chain/cochain complex with coefficients G = h0(point), provided hn(point) = 0 for n ≠ 0 (homology case) or the analogous hypothesis for cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key checks: cellular chain groups are direct sums (homology) or products (cohomology) of copies of G; boundary/coboundary maps are determined by degrees of attaching maps S^n → S^n and the lemma on additivity ensures degrees act correctly. This yields isomorphisms hn(X) ≈ Hn(X;G) (or H^n for cohomology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree action criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A map S^n → S^n of degree m induces multiplication by m on hn(S^n) ≈ G (in any homology theory satisfying the axioms), and degree is additive with respect to the sum operation in πn(S^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verifying degree behavior for degrees 0 and 1 and using additivity (Lemma 4.60) gives the general case. This fact is used to identify cellular boundary maps between copies of G with the ordinary cellular boundary maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely supported coboundary maps for infinite cell complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: When a CW complex has infinitely many cells in a given dimension, the cellular coboundary maps in a cohomology theory are still determined factorwise because attaching maps have compact image and meet only finitely many lower-dimensional cells (i.e. the induced maps are finitely supported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This finitely supported property ensures that maps from product groups are determined by their restrictions to finitely many factors, allowing identification of cellular coboundary maps in the generalized theory with those in ordinary cohomology with coefficients G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental class in H^n(K(G,n);G)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a distinguished class α ∈ H^n(K(G,n); G) (the fundamental class) given by the inverse of the Hurewicz isomorphism πn(K(G,n)) ≅ Hn(K; Z); concretely represented by the cellular cochain assigning to each n-cell the element of πn(K(G,n)) determined by its characteristic map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The natural transformation T: [X, K(G,n)] → H^n(X;G) has the form T([f]) = f^*(α). Choosing K(G,n) with (n−1)-skeleton a point makes the description concrete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milnor theorem usage: loopspace CW type
rubrics_metrics.description: The loopspace ΩX of a CW complex X has the homotopy type of a CW complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is used to justify working with ΩKn+1 as CW complexes (or CW approximations) so that weak homotopy equivalences Kn → ΩKn+1 can be treated within the CW category and the homotopy-theoretic constructions behave well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectrum ⇒ reduced cohomology theory theorem (Thm 4.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: If {Kn} is an Ω–spectrum then the functors X ↦ hn(X) = h(X, Kn), n ∈ Z, define a reduced cohomology theory on basepointed CW complexes and basepoint-preserving maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof outline: verify homotopy and wedge axioms, and produce long exact sequences via the Puppe construction and the weak equivalences Kn→ΩKn+1; naturality and abelian group structure follow from iterated loopspace structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brown representability (converse assertion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversely, every reduced cohomology theory on CW complexes arises from an Ω–spectrum (the Brown representability theorem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as the remarkable converse and is to be proved later in the text (§4.E); it justifies that the spectrum description captures all reduced cohomology theories on CW complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification H^n(X;G) ≅ [X, K(G,n)] (Thm 4.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are natural bijections T : [X, K(G,n)] → H^n(X; G) for all CW complexes X and n>0; T([f]) = f^*(α) for a distinguished fundamental class α ∈ H^n(K(G,n); G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof proceeds by showing hn(X) = [X, K(G,n)] defines a reduced cohomology theory with correct coefficient groups, then applying the general uniqueness theorem (Theorem 4.59) to identify it with ordinary cohomology; the explicit α comes from the Hurewicz isomorphism.
